Wind speed at 2 m above short grass

Source: R/forcing-derived.R
ef_wind_2m.Rd

Converts the wind speed measured at a given height above the ground to the wind speed at 2 m with the logarithmic wind profile of FAO-56, valid for measurements above a short grass surface. It is the wind speed entering the reference evapotranspiration (ef_ref_et()).

Usage

ef_wind_2m(wind_speed, height)

Arguments

wind_speed

Numeric. Wind speed measured at height \(u_z\) [m s-1]. Must be finite and >= 0.

height

Numeric. Height of the measurement above the ground \(z\) [m]. Must be finite and greater than 6.42 / 67.8 = 0.0947 m, where the logarithm becomes non-positive.

Value

A numeric vector of wind speed at 2 m \(u_2\) [m s-1] with the common length of the inputs, keeping their dim.

Details

$$u_2 = u_z \frac{4.87}{\ln(67.8 z - 5.42)}$$ (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 47). At height = 2 the factor is 1.00022, not exactly 1 (FAO-56 annex 2, table 2.9 rounds it to 1.000); at 10 m it is 0.74795 (table 2.9: 0.748).

Assumption (FAO-56): logarithmic profile for measurements above a short grass surface. This is not the extrapolation to the blending height of METRIC, which uses the roughness of the station surface and the raw station wind (ef_blending_wind()).

Missing values propagate. Negative wind speeds, heights <= 0.0947 m or infinite values raise earthflux_domain_error.

Verification status

VERIFICADA (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 47; cases V12 and V13). The same equation is ASCE-EWRI (2005) Eq. 33 (p. 26) and Eq. 67 (p. 44; the text on that page calls it "Eq. 68", a typographical error), for measurements above clipped grass; the report directs wind measured above other surfaces (e.g. alfalfa) to its Appendix B, not implemented here.

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The ASCE Standardized Reference Evapotranspiration Equation. Task Committee on Standardization of Reference Evapotranspiration, Environmental and Water Resources Institute of the American Society of Civil Engineers. Final report, January 2005. Published as Allen, R. G., Walter, I. A., Elliott, R. L., Howell, T. A., Itenfisu, D., Jensen, M. E., & Snyder, R. L. (Eds.), American Society of Civil Engineers, Reston, VA. doi:10.1061/9780784408056

See also

Other derived meteorological variables: ef_dewpoint(), ef_ea, ef_es(), ef_es_slope(), ef_psychrometric(), ef_ra_daily(), ef_ra_period(), ef_rso()

Examples

# FAO-56 example 14: 3.2 m s-1 measured at 10 m
ef_wind_2m(wind_speed = 3.2, height = 10)
#> [1] 2.393443
